_source:
A real 'Music Arts (Musical Arts) Form 2 Scheme of Work' (a real Zambian secondary school's own department) was shared with this project via Drive, as three separate real documents -- one per term (Term 1, Term 2, Term 3), with no duplicate re-uploads identified among them. A teacher's name and school name were found in the header of every one of these documents and are not reproduced here per this app's standing sourcing policy. This is a genuine gap fill -- this app previously had no Music Form 2 content at all (only Form 1 Term 3). The source PDFs are titled 'MUSICAL ARTS' / 'MUSIC ARTS' throughout; this is the same subject as this app's existing 'Music' (code MUS) entries. Cites the real official '2024 Music Arts Syllabus, Ordinary Secondary Education Form 1-4' with real page citations (pp.8-11).

A genuine structural feature of the source is preserved rather than silently corrected: sub-topic 2.1.1 (Zambian Music Styles) is taught across two consecutive weeks under two different specific-competence rows (Zambian styles, then foreign influences on Zambian music) both carrying the same 2.1.1 code -- these are combined into one sub-topic entry here rather than duplicated. Likewise Topic 2.13 (Musical Arts and Technology) spans the Term 2/Term 3 boundary: its first sub-topic (2.13.1 Music Writing) is taught in Term 2, and its second (2.13.2 Music Recording) in the first week of Term 3 -- each is placed in the term where the source actually teaches it, under the same real topic number.

The remainder of Term 3 (weeks 2-11 of the real scheme) is a genuine, honestly-documented gap rather than fabricated content: after week 1's Music Recording sub-topic, the source's own remaining Term 3 weeks are 'PRACTICAL PROJECT' (composition, recording and a conducted group performance), 'REVISION', 'THEORY ASSESSMENT', 'PRACTICAL ASSESSMENT', 'PROJECT SUBMISSION & REVIEW', 'CAREER EXPLORATION' (music industry careers), and 'SYLLABUS OVERVIEW' (a preview of Form 3 topics) -- the source's own Prescribed Competences column is marked 'N/A' for every one of these rows, meaning they apply or assess the topics already covered rather than introduce any new numbered syllabus topic of their own. No separate Term 3 topic is invented here to fill that real gap.

Its own Content/Concept, Learning Activities, Strategies/Methods and Materials/Resources columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for every other bundled subject in this app.

subject.name: Music
subject.description: Music (Musical Arts) syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre, 2024).

grade.name: Form 2
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 2" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

sub_topics.name: 2.1.1 Zambian Music Styles
sub_topics.description: Identifying Zambian music styles (traditional, Kalindula, Zamrock, contemporary) and foreign influences (instruments, attire, technology) on Zambian music.

competencies.description: Identify different Zambian music styles (traditional, Kalindula, Zamrock, contemporary) and select Zambian music for performance
Discuss foreign influences on Zambian music (instruments, attire, technology) and perform Zambian musical styles

sub_topics.name: 2.2.1 Compound Metre
sub_topics.description: Identifying compound time signatures (e.g. 6/8, 9/8, 12/8) and demonstrating compound time in a composition.

competencies.description: Apply compound time (compound duple, compound triple, compound quadruple) in a composition

sub_topics.name: 2.3.1 C Clefs
sub_topics.description: Relating letter names to pitch levels on the alto and tenor (C) clefs, and relating the C clefs to instruments such as viola.

competencies.description: Relate pitch to the C clefs (alto and tenor)

sub_topics.name: 2.3.2 Double Sharps and Double Flats
sub_topics.description: The function and effect of double accidentals in a music composition.

competencies.description: Apply double sharps and double flats in a music composition

sub_topics.name: 2.4.1 Compound Intervals
sub_topics.description: Intervals larger than an octave, described by numerical value.

competencies.description: Apply compound intervals in a music composition

sub_topics.name: 2.5.1 Melody Writing
sub_topics.description: Techniques for composing a longer melody (motif, phrasing, starting and ending).

competencies.description: Construct an eight-bar melody

sub_topics.name: 2.5.2 Transposing
sub_topics.description: Transposing a melody to a new key (by key, interval or clef).

competencies.description: Transpose a diatonic melody

sub_topics.name: 2.5.3 Translating
sub_topics.description: Translating between staff notation and tonic sol-fa, and punctuating rhythmic expressions (full-stop, comma, colon, semicolon).

competencies.description: Translate a diatonic melody from staff notation to tonic sol-fa notation and vice versa

sub_topics.name: 2.5.4 Sight Reading
sub_topics.description: Sight-reading skills in treble, bass, alto, and tenor clefs.

competencies.description: Perform music written in any clef (C clef, G clef, F clef) using voice or instrument

sub_topics.name: 2.6.1 Structure of Rondo
sub_topics.description: Detecting rhythmic and melodic contrast in rondo form (ABACA).

competencies.description: Construct melody in rondo form, including sections of equal and unequal length in rondo design

sub_topics.name: 2.7.1 Advanced Musical Signs
sub_topics.description: Interpreting advanced musical signs (D.C. al fine, fermata, accent, slur).

competencies.description: Interpret advanced musical signs (D.C. al fine, fermata, accent, slur) in a score

sub_topics.name: 2.8.1 Chord Progression
sub_topics.description: Identifying common chord progressions (e.g. I-IV-V-I) using Roman numeral analysis.

competencies.description: Identify chord progressions

sub_topics.name: 2.8.2 Types of Cadences
sub_topics.description: Detecting harmonic cadences in major keys: perfect, imperfect, plagal, interrupted.

competencies.description: Detect harmonic cadences in major keys

sub_topics.name: 2.8.3 Part Singing
sub_topics.description: Singing in harmony with others.

competencies.description: Perform two-, three- and four-part scores in group singing

sub_topics.name: 2.9.1 Density
sub_topics.description: Textural types: monophonic, polyphonic, homophonic.

competencies.description: Identify density for a given piece of music

sub_topics.name: 2.10.1 Conducting Figures
sub_topics.description: Conducting patterns for duple, triple, and quadruple time, and relating music accentuation to hand movements (downbeat, upbeat, syncopation, dynamic changes, subtle accent).

competencies.description: Recognise types of conducting figures (duple, triple, quadruple)
Relate music accentuation to hand movements in conducting

sub_topics.name: 2.11.1 Singing
sub_topics.description: Advanced singing techniques: breath control, posture, articulation, diction, projection.

competencies.description: Apply singing techniques

sub_topics.name: 2.12.1 Instrument Playing Techniques
sub_topics.description: Developing technique on a chosen instrument, through individual practice and group ensemble playing.

competencies.description: Apply instrument playing techniques on a chosen instrument

sub_topics.name: 2.13.1 Music Writing
sub_topics.description: Identifying available music notation software (e.g. MuseScore), discussing its features, determining the kind of software to use, and writing music using it.

competencies.description: Write music using software

sub_topics.name: 2.13.2 Music Recording
sub_topics.description: Basic principles of audio recording: identifying available recording devices (phones, recorders, microphones) and discussing their features.

competencies.description: Record music
